metadata.title: One Brief, One Trace.
metadata.note: Project update (single change): Langfuse trace grouping. Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'Vendor Intelligence'. The reusable lesson: trace the RUN, not the model. ONE insight: the tracer was attached to the model, and get_llm() builds a fresh model per call, so one brief logged ~20 disconnected flat traces; attaching the handler once to the graph invocation gives one nested trace. Bookends render (composer/verdict/handoff/outro via Claude Remotion comps); body B01-B04 are house-style 4K PIL cards generated by make_cards.py. DOUBLE-CHECK LAW — exact facts from the creator's change log: ~20 disconnected traces all named 'ChatBedrockConverse'; cause = callback on the model + get_llm() rebuilds the model per call; get_llm() no longer attaches a callback; new trace_config() builds the run config with the handler, a 'brief:{company}' name, and metadata; supervisor.py:503 passes it to graph.invoke(); result = one trace with 92 nested observations instead of 20 flat rows; tool calls now traced (never before).

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. My tracing was quietly useless. One brief was producing about twenty separate traces, all with the same generic name, and the tool calls weren't showing up at all. The fix was small, and it came down to one idea: where you attach the tracer.

props.command: Why is one brief logging ~20 disconnected traces — and why are the tool calls missing?

beats.narration_text: Here's what I was seeing. A single brief, broken into roughly twenty disconnected traces. Every one just labeled ChatBedrockConverse, the model's default name. No nesting, no sense of what called what. And the tool calls, the actual work, never appeared in the trace at all. Useless for the one question tracing exists to answer: what happened?

card.title: Twenty Traces, One Brief.
card.subtitle: tracing that couldn't answer “what happened?”
card.caption: one logical task, scattered across twenty unrelated rows
card.footer: A TRACE YOU CAN'T READ IS NOT OBSERVABILITY

beats.narration_text: The cause is the interesting part. The tracer was attached to the model. But the code builds a fresh model on every single call. So every call spun up a new model, with a new tracer, and logged its own separate trace. The fix, in one idea: don't attach the tracer to the model, attach it to the run, the whole graph invocation, once.

show.event: the left column builds: per-model → many traces
the right column resolves: one run, one tree (accent)

card.title: Where You Attach It.
card.subtitle: the whole bug, in one choice
card.caption: get_llm() builds a new model every call — so a per-model tracer logs one trace per call
card.footer: TRACE THE RUN, NOT THE MODEL

beats.narration_text: In code, three small changes. get_llm stops attaching the callback. A new trace_config builds the run's config, the handler, a name, brief colon company, and metadata. And the supervisor passes that config into graph dot invoke. One tracer, scoped to the whole run, instead of one per model.

show.event: the three change cards snap in

card.title: The Fix, in Three.
card.subtitle: three small changes
card.caption: one tracer, built into the run config — not into a model that gets rebuilt
card.footer: DROP THE CALLBACK · CONFIG THE RUN · PASS IT IN

beats.narration_text: The difference: before, twenty flat, nameless rows. After, one trace, named for the company, with ninety-two nested observations showing the real call tree. And for the first time, the tool calls are in there. Same run, finally legible.

show.event: the brief feeds the run config into Langfuse

card.title: One Trace, 92 Observations.
card.subtitle: the same brief, now legible
card.answer: 1 trace · 92 nested observations · tool calls traced (first time)
card.caption: before: 20 flat rows · after: one named tree you can actually read
card.footer: 20 FLAT → 1 TREE OF 92 · TOOL CALLS VISIBLE

beats.narration_text: The lesson: trace the run, not the model, especially when the model gets rebuilt on every call. Attach your observability once, at the top, and name it something you can actually find later.

artifactLines: The Langfuse callback was attached to the model — and get_llm() builds a fresh model every call.
So each call logged its own flat trace: ~20 disconnected rows, all named “ChatBedrockConverse.”
Fix: get_llm() drops the callback; a new trace_config() carries the handler + brief:{company} + metadata; supervisor passes it to graph.invoke().
Result: one trace with 92 nested observations (not 20 flat rows), and tool calls traced for the first time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Open your own tracing dashboard. Is one logical task showing up as one trace, or as a scatter of disconnected ones? If it's scattered, find where the handler is attached, and ask whether that object gets rebuilt on every call. That's usually the whole bug.
